case_name: Sandeep and another v State of Haryana
respondent:
State of Haryana
Supreme Court of India

26  May  2015
Cr.A. No. 1554 of 2014
(Non-Reportable)
The Judgment was delivered by : Uday Umesh Lalit, J.
1. This appeal by Special Leave by appellants, Sandeep and his mother Krishna, challenges the judgment and order dated 18.09.2012 passed by the High Court of Punjab and Haryana at Chandigarh in Criminal Appeal No. D-203-DB/2008 affirming their conviction under Sections 304-B, 498A read with S. 34 IPC.
2. The crime in the instant case was registered on the basis of statement made by Sharmila, wife of appellant Sandeep, to Suresh Chand, ASI at 6:15 p.m. on 2.11.2006. Her statement Ext. P-13 was to the following effect:-
"Stated that I am resident of aforesaid address. I was married to Sandeep S/o Rajbir @Raja Jat by caste r/o Ghikara on 21.05.2005. After some days of the marriage I was kept properly and there after they started harassing me and saying that less dowry is brought. My husband, my mother-in-law, Krishna fath
facts: The crime was registered on the basis of a statement made by Sharmila, wife of Sandeep, to Suresh Chand, ASI at 6:15 p.m. on 2.11.2006.
The appellants were tried for having committed the offence under Sections 304-B, 498-A read with S. 34 IPC in the court of Sessions Judge, Bhiwani.
The trial court found that the prosecution had proved its case against the appellants but gave benefit of doubt to accused Rajbir and acquitted him of all the offences.
The High Court affirmed the order of conviction but reduced the sentence under Section 304-B read with S. 34 IPC to ten years and set aside the sentence of fine under said count.
issues: Whether the conviction in the present case rested solely on two dying declarations, which were not consistent with each other
Whether there were loopholes in the dying declarations rendering them unworthy of reliance
petitioner_arguments: The conviction in the present case rested solely on two dying declarations, which were not consistent with each other
There were loopholes in the dying declarations rendering them unworthy of reliance
The Doctor who had given the certificate of fitness to record such dying declaration was not examined at all
Given the fact that Sharmila had suffered 85% to 90% burns it would be impossible for her to have given such statements
At the first available opportunity said Sharmila had not stated anything regarding the incident or the involvement of the appellant before PW 7
The evidence as regards alleged demand for dowry was absolutely scanty
respondent_arguments: Both the dying declarations were consistent as regards the involvement of the present appellants
Dying declaration Ext. P-6 recorded by the Judicial Magistrate in the presence of the Doctor and with requisite certification from the Doctor was entitled to be given absolute credence

The dying declarations Ext. P-13 and P-6 themselves stated about the demands for dowry and inability to fulfill such demands being the reason why she was set afire which was fully supported by the testimony of PW9
court_reasoning: A dying declaration made by person on the verge of his death has a special sanctity as at that solemn moment, a person is most unlikely to make any untrue statement.
The shadow of impending death is by itself the guarantee of the truth of the statement made by the deceased regarding the causes or circumstances leading to his death.
holding: Both the dying declarations were consistent with each other in material particulars

The trial court sentenced the appellants to undergo life imprisonment and to pay fine of Rs. 10000/- each for the offence punishable under Section 304-B read with S. 34 IPC and in default of payment of fine to undergo further rigorous imprisonment of two years.
